digest.component_or_area: plan review det floor — blocking vs advisory check extraction
propositions: det_floor.py (793 LOC) exceeds the 800-LOC hard cap by 7 lines; the retained half after extraction must reach ~550 LOC to restore headroom

Four never-blocking advisory checks (p2_resolution, p3_package_existence, p6_ac_quality, p7_destructive) plus their private regex constants form a closed call cluster with zero inbound or outbound edges to the remaining checks that stay

Module-object bindings in test suite (monkeypatches on det_floor.DET_CHECKS, det_floor.run_det_floor, det_floor.est_tokens, and name imports of _clarity_score/_count_ac_items/_description_limit) all target symbols in the retained half, so test patches continue reaching live code after the split

p6_ac_quality calls vague_hits_in_line, _lint_verify_command, and _verify_command_strings as bare names bound by det_floor's module-level imports; moving p6 to det_advisory.py requires mirroring those imports in the new module and dropping them from det_floor.py
Complexity baseline and module-size registry contain no path-keyed entries for det_floor.py, so no moved symbol carries a frozen ceiling and no ratchet can report regress

Three prior splits (det_clarity.py extracting p10/p11, det_lint.py extracting p9, and this one) all use the same cycle-avoidance contract: from __future__ import annotations + TYPE_CHECKING for DetResult/PlanContext, plus lazy from .det_floor import DetResult in function bodies
